title: Sell Mineral Rights in Worthington, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Worthington, WV | Marion County
metaDescription: Worthington sits near Fairmont in Marion County. We trace the deed record across generations of family ownership and buy mineral interests.
heroLead: Worthington is small, but the mineral interests scattered under its older tracts have usually passed through more hands than the town's population would suggest.
intro: Sitting just outside Fairmont, Worthington's mineral history is tied to Marion County's long run of coal and gas activity, with many tracts here severed decades before anyone was thinking about Marcellus economics. What a given Worthington family actually owns today — coal, gas, both, or neither — depends entirely on how those old deeds were written, not on assumption.

We pull the Marion County record to trace that history for a specific Worthington tract: what was severed, when, and how the interest has passed since, generation by generation, before we discuss any number.

sections.heading: Worthington and the Marion County Record
paragraphs: The Marion County Clerk's office in Fairmont holds the deed book covering Worthington, and tracts here often carry a longer paper trail than their small size would suggest — multiple conveyances, a coal severance from one era, a gas lease from another, and estate filings layered across several generations of the same family.
We read that full trail rather than stopping at whatever document an owner happens to have in a drawer at home.

sections.heading: Position on the Marcellus Flank
paragraphs: Worthington sits closer to the flank of Marion County's Marcellus activity than to the dense pad development found in counties like Harrison or Doddridge, which affects how we approach valuation. Legacy production and the possibility of future development both factor in, but neither should be assumed without checking the specific tract.
We look at well and permit history near your particular parcel rather than valuing based on the county's reputation alone.

sections.heading: Converting an Old Flat-Rate Lease Near Fairmont
paragraphs: Some Worthington-area leases date back to a period well before the Marcellus era and pay a fixed flat rate with no connection to current production. If a modern well has since been drilled under a spacing unit that includes your tract, that lease may be required to convert to at least West Virginia's 1/8 statutory royalty.
We check this on every file, because the difference between an old flat payment and a converted royalty interest is often the difference between a modest offer and a substantial one.

sections.heading: Heirship Across Generations in Worthington
paragraphs: It's common for a Worthington mineral interest to have passed through three or four generations without ever being formally divided on paper, leaving a group of cousins each holding an undivided fraction they may not fully understand. We've worked through estates here that were never taken through fiduciary supervisor proceedings at all.
We handle that tracing directly and buy individual fractional interests from a single heir, without requiring the rest of the family to participate in the sale.

faqs.question: How do I find out what my family actually owns under a Worthington property?
faqs.answer: We trace the Marion County deed record to confirm exactly what was severed and how it passed down, which tells us specifically what interest, if any, you hold.

faqs.question: Our old lease pays a small flat rate every year. Should that have changed by now?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether a well covered by the statute is currently producing under a unit that includes your tract. We check the lease and well record before answering that for your specific situation.

faqs.question: The estate that should have divided our family's mineral rights was never formally settled. Can you still work with us?
faqs.answer: Yes, unsettled and partially settled estates are common on older Marion County tracts, and we regularly trace ownership through that kind of history.
